subject: surgery
title: Parathyroid Adenoma, Sestamibi Scintigraphy, and Focused Parathyroidectomy

steps.tx: Autonomous oversecretion of parathyroid hormone produces the endocrine syndrome known as primary hyperparathyroidism. In over eighty-five percent of cases, primary hyperparathyroidism is caused by a benign, solitary **parathyroid adenoma**. Parathyroid gland four-gland hyperplasia accounts for ten to twelve percent, multiple adenomas occur in three to four percent, and parathyroid carcinoma develops in less than one percent. Adenomas arise predominantly from mutations in the cyclin D1 gene or MEN1 tumor suppressor.
steps.say: A solitary parathyroid adenoma causes over eighty-five percent of primary hyperparathyroidism cases, while four-gland hyperplasia accounts for ten to twelve percent.

steps.tx: The biochemical hallmark of primary hyperparathyroidism is persistent hypercalcaemia in the presence of inappropriately elevated or non-suppressed intact parathyroid hormone. While modern patients frequently present with asymptomatic hypercalcaemia detected on routine biochemical screening, classical untreated disease manifests with the traditional surgical mnemonic **bones, stones, abdominal groans, and psychic moans**. Skeletal involvement produces subperiosteal bone resorption, osteoporosis, and bone cysts termed osteitis fibrosa cystica.
steps.say: Primary hyperparathyroidism is diagnosed by hypercalcaemia with inappropriately high parathyroid hormone. Classical untreated disease presents as bones, stones, abdominal groans, and psychiatric moans.

steps.tx: Preoperative imaging in primary hyperparathyroidism is designed strictly for surgical localization to facilitate minimally invasive exploration, never to diagnose hyperparathyroidism, which is established biochemically. The preeminent radionuclide imaging modality is **technetium-99m sestamibi scintigraphy**. Sestamibi is concentrated by mitochondria within both thyroid and parathyroid tissue, but is washed out rapidly from thyroid parenchyma while being selectively retained within the hyperactive, oxyphil-rich mitochondria of parathyroid adenomas.
steps.say: Preoperative imaging localizes the adenoma for targeted surgery. Sestamibi scintigraphy washes out rapidly from normal thyroid but is retained in the mitochondria of parathyroid adenomas.

nodes.label: Early Phase (15 Min): Diffuse Thyroid & Parathyroid Uptake
Differential Rapid Washout from Normal Thyroid Tissue
Delayed Phase (2 Hours): Persistent Focal Retention in Adenoma

steps.tx: Combining technetium-99m sestamibi SPECT-CT with high-resolution neck ultrasound constitutes the gold standard dual-modality localization algorithm, achieving concordance in over eighty-five percent of patients. On ultrasonography, a parathyroid adenoma presents as an oval, sharply circumscribed, markedly **hypoechoic nodule with peripheral vascular arc** situated immediately posterior to the thyroid lobe. For discordant cases, four-dimensional computed tomography (4D-CT) provides definitive multiplanar anatomical localization.
steps.say: Combining Sestamibi scintigraphy with high-resolution ultrasound provides eighty-five percent localization accuracy. Four-dimensional CT resolves discordant cases by mapping vascular perfusion.

left.title: Technetium-99m Sestamibi SPECT
points: Superb for identifying ectopic adenomas in mediastinum
Delayed phase retention confirms parathyroid origin
Limited resolution in small (<500 mg) adenomas

right.title: Four-Dimensional CT (4D-CT)
points: Parathyroid adenomas show rapid arterial wash-in and wash-out
Exceptional spatial resolution for reoperative neck surgery
Delivers higher radiation dose to the thyroid bed

steps.tx: When preoperative imaging convincingly localizes a solitary adenoma, the surgeon performs a **minimally invasive parathyroidectomy**. Through a focused two-to-three-centimetre incision over the localized quadrant, the adenoma is mobilized and excised while preserving the remaining three normal parathyroid glands. Compared to historical four-gland bilateral neck exploration, focused parathyroidectomy significantly reduces operative duration, postoperative pain, and risk of recurrent laryngeal nerve injury.
steps.say: Minimally invasive parathyroidectomy excises the localized adenoma through a small focused incision, reducing surgical trauma and recovery time compared to open four-gland exploration.

steps.tx: The technological keystone ensuring curative success during focused parathyroidectomy is rapid **intraoperative parathyroid hormone monitoring**. Because parathyroid hormone possesses an exceptionally brief serum half-life of merely three to five minutes, successful excision of the hyperfunctioning adenoma is followed by a precipitous decline in circulating intact PTH. Peripheral venous blood samples are drawn at baseline prior to incision, immediately upon gland excision, and at five and ten minutes post-excision.
steps.say: Because parathyroid hormone has a half-life of under five minutes, successfully removing the adenoma triggers a rapid fall in circulating PTH measured in the operating room.

left.title: Rapid Intraoperative PTH Assay
points: Reports definitive quantitative hormone levels within 15 minutes
Assesses systemic hormonal clearance in real time
Confirms complete surgical cure before patient wakes

right.title: Frozen Section Histology
points: Examines structural cellular composition under microscope
Distinguishes parathyroid tissue from lymph node or thyroid
Cannot differentiate an adenoma from multiglandular hyperplasia
Does not confirm biochemical cure or absence of second adenoma

steps.tx: Surgical cure is validated in the operating theater using the established **Miami criterion for parathyroidectomy**. The Miami criterion dictates that a drop in intraoperative intact parathyroid hormone of fifty percent or greater from the highest pre-incision or pre-excision baseline value, measured ten minutes after gland resection, confirms complete excision of all hyperfunctioning tissue. If the PTH level fails to drop by fifty percent, the surgeon immediately converts the procedure to bilateral four-gland exploration.
steps.say: Under the Miami criterion, a drop in parathyroid hormone exceeding fifty percent ten minutes after excision confirms surgical cure. Failure to drop dictates four-gland bilateral exploration.

nodes.label: PTH Drop > 50%: Confirms Complete Cure & Conclude Surgery

steps.tx: Following successful parathyroidectomy in patients with severe, longstanding osteitis fibrosa cystica, sudden withdrawal of high parathyroid hormone triggers **hungry bone syndrome**. Characterized by profound, prolonged hypocalcaemia and hypophosphataemia, avid remineralization of demineralized skeletal matrix ravenously consumes circulating calcium and phosphate. Management demands aggressive, continuous intravenous calcium infusion, active calcitriol, and oral calcium carbonate for weeks until bone remineralization equilibrates.
steps.say: Hungry bone syndrome develops after surgery in severe bone disease when demineralized skeleton rapidly absorbs circulating calcium and phosphate, requiring aggressive calcium therapy.

rows: Elevated hyperphosphataemia (loss of renal PTH phosphaturia)
Massive calcium infusions and high-dose oral calcitriol
Standard oral calcium and low-dose calcitriol titration
